title: Borrowing
description:
Write these functions with the right kind of reference:

```rust
fn add_score(scores: &mut Vec<u32>, score: u32) -> usize     // adds the score, returns the new count
fn best<'a>(scores: &'a Vec<u32>) -> Option<&'a u32>         // a reference to the highest score (the first on a tie)
fn normalize(words: &mut Vec<String>)                         // trims and lower-cases each word in place
fn swap_ends(values: &mut Vec<i32>)                           // swaps the first and last items (if there are at least two)
fn count_starting(words: &Vec<String>, prefix: &str) -> usize // ignoring case
```

The `'a` in `best` says the returned reference points into `scores`; lesson 4.04 explains it. (Lesson 2.03 shows how slices let functions like these accept arrays and parts of vectors too.)
hints: `best` returns a reference into the vector, not a copy: start with `&scores[0]`, loop over `scores` (which gives `&u32` items) and remember the reference to the largest. An `Option<&u32>` is `Some(reference)` or `None` (lesson 2.05 covers `Option`): return `None` for an empty vector.

`for w in words.iter_mut()` gives each item as a `&mut String`. To replace it, assign to `*w`: `*w = w.trim().to_lowercase();`. For `swap_ends`, copy `values[0]` into a variable before overwriting it.
